It's Halo, c'mon now, do I need to give a reason for you to play Halo 1, 2, 3, 4, and Reach? ESPECIALLY 3 AND REACH!

So, Halo. The legendary series known far and wide that singlehandedly sold millions of Xboxes. In spite of the series eventually being handed off to 343 and put through the world's slowest suicide, the first 4 games are still universally beloved to this day. Unfortunately though, as someone who never grew up with them with no hype to cloud my vision, the series is just good and not great. You can respect something for its innovations and what it did to the industry, but the games themselves are extremely basic, poorly balanced shooters that were just vehicles to sell the multiplayer. They're not bad by any stretch, but compared to many many other shooters that came later, time has not been kind to them. These games also lose points in my eyes for prototyping things like sitting in cover doing nothing to recharge your shields in the gameplay, and snarky, arrogant and insufferable girlbosses (at least 1 per game) in the story. (But mercifully [spoiler] half of the latter do get killed off. [/spoiler] )

Halo: CE: The game that started it all. Clunky voice acting, an extremely basic story that completely shifts gears halfway through and a sombre ending that gets retconned immediately, mixed with a combat system with nothing really to offer veterans of the genre. All of the enemies are ridiculous damage sponges, to the point where it feels like every gun but the sniper, shotgun and rocket launcher shoot feathers. The level design is horrible, with hour long levels where you walk through the same 3 rooms and hallways over and over and over again followed by massive open areas with no cover, with enemy placements that feel like the devs just tossed 10 enemies into an enclosed space and called it a day. The checkpoints are extremely far apart, with a single random grenade falling off a grunt one-shotting you and costing you minutes of progress for no reason. You have a flimsy health bar that doesn't recharge like the rest of the series, and health packs are unbelievably sparce. I normally play shooters on hard mode, but I had to switch to normal to have any enjoyment whatsoever without my badass armored super-soldier dying from a stiff breeze.

Halo 2: marked improvements to the gameplay (like dual-wielding) and story, but still nothing groundbreaking. You actually find out who and what the covenant are in-game without being forced to read a book, and it's actually compelling. Playing as Arbiter for half the game is novel, but him and chief are nearly identical in every way apart from flashlight/cloak, so they feel more similar than they should. Guns still shoot feathers and the enemies are still stupidly tanky, and in the latter half of the game, nearly all of the enemies are brutes, which makes the tankiness even worse. The game also had an extremely troubled production back in the day, and as such, the game just ends on a massive cliffhanger basically out of nowhere.

Halo 3: The best game in terms of gameplay and story. Guns actually feel marginally powerful, and combat gadgets allow you to get more creative with your gameplay and positioning. The levels are well designed, combat feels good, the locales are varied, and the story comes to a pretty satisfying conclusion assuming you deem everything afterward non-canon like most fans do.

ODST: a brief spinoff that takes place between 2 and 3 starring a crack team of boring jabronies. Half the game is spent wandering through the same 3 dark, empty streets as a silent protag, maybe shooting 2 or 3 enemies before going into a flashback that plays out like a proper mission. (A very short mission, and then it's back to wandering in the dark again for the same amount of time.) It is PAINFULLY boring, and it's a story that didn't need to be told as the only thing you learn is that [spoiler] the snail-iens that you've been shooting all game are actually snail-frens. [/spoiler] That's it. Master Chief is not even mentioned once, and you only briefly hear from one of the jabroni squad again in Reach. Completely pointless.

Halo: Reach: A prequel to CE. The gameplay is "modernized" for lack of a better term, with the gimmick being armor abilities like sprinting, cloak and invincibility instead of them being powerups. The gameplay is about tied with 3 in terms of quality, and all of the characters don't get nearly enough dialogue or screentime for me to care about any of them. The game is mostly famous for its ending and how it immediately leads into the first game, but apart from that it's a pretty unncessessary prequel that still doesn't even explain why the covenent are at war with humanity in the first place. Best get reading, [I] idiot. [/I]

Halo 4: I didn't play it. I've heard that everything after 3 sucks and the story careens off a cliff, so I'm not wasting my time.

There are far worse shooters out there, and if you want to see how the genre were revolutionized back in the day, they are still enjoyable. They are still good games that paved the way for what came after, but without growing up with them, they don't even come close to my favorites of the genre.

You know what's funny? Half the gaming industry is still trying to figure out how to make shooters as good as these.

Six Halo games in one collection, and the campaigns alone make this worth owning. Great stories, fantastic music, memorable missions, and gunplay that somehow still feels right after all these years.

Halo 3 is still brilliant, Reach hits differently, and the original trilogy deserves every bit of its reputation. Even the games I like less have something worth experiencing.

It's not all perfect. Some levels haven't aged particularly well, Halo 4 is a bit of a divisive one, and those bloody Jackal snipers in Halo 2 can still go fuck themselves.

But I love having all these campaigns together on PC, without needing to dig out an old console.

Funny how games from twenty years ago can remind you what you've been missing in modern shooters.

[h1]RECOMMENDED. THANKS TO PEOPLE WHO DON'T WORK FOR MICROSOFT.[/h1]

[b]An open letter to Pierre Hintze, Vice President and Studio Head of Halo Studios (formerly 343 Industries).[/b]

Pierre,

How fucking embarrassing is Project Reclaimer for you people?

I'm genuinely curious.

People are buying Halo: The Master Chief Collection specifically to play a community-built version of Halo 3 instead of launching MCC itself.

[b]You're selling people the files they need to avoid your own product.[/b]

I've loved Halo 3 since I was eight years old. I've watched this franchise spend the better part of two decades squandering its potential while fans repeatedly explained what they wanted.

Dedicated servers. Proper server browsing. Expanded Forge. More customization. Even something as hilariously trivial as lowering your fucking weapon in multiplayer.

Apparently, we were asking too much.

Then some enthusiasts got together and started implementing this shit themselves. For free. Without Microsoft's budget. Without an entire corporate hierarchy collecting salaries to discuss the future of Halo.

And somehow, it runs beautifully.

[b]What the fuck have you people been doing?[/b]

Seriously. I'd love to hear the explanation. How does a community project manage to make Halo 3 feel more alive than the company responsible for maintaining the franchise?

You're the head of Halo Studios. Surely someone has brought this up in a meeting. Has anybody had the balls to ask why fans are getting more excited about an unofficial Halo 3 client than the official product?

Or is everyone too busy rebranding the studio again?

[hr][/hr]

[b]To anyone reading this review:[/b]

Buy MCC on Steam. Install Halo 3. Then visit [url=https://projectreclaimer.dev/]Project Reclaimer[/url].

The community has done some incredible work, and they deserve your support.

As for Halo Studios, congratulations on finally giving people a compelling reason to purchase MCC.

[b]Someone else made better use of it.[/b]

[spoiler]Please don't send Project Reclaimer a cease-and-desist. It would be nice if Microsoft could manage to leave one good thing alone.[/spoiler]
